newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia copper cable market to show strong growth.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia copper cable market to show strong growth.

text.p: Malaysia's use of copper will rise substantially into the 21st Century due to major power and telecommunications projects which will sustain strong demand for copper cable, analysts and industry experts said on Friday.

"It's quite conservative to estimate that at least 100,000 tonnes of copper will be needed locally over the next five years to meet cabling needs for telecommunication and infrastructure projects," said Patrick Lim, analyst at Jupiter Securities.

Malaysian government statistics show that the value of locally-made wire and wire products jumped 27.4 percent in the first six months of 1996 to 402.79 million ringgit ($161.12 million) against 316.22 million ringgit in the same 1995 period.

Power utility Tenaga Nasional is expected to spend five billion ringgit between 1997 and 2000, or an average of $1.0 billion yearly, on copper cables for its power generation needs, industry officials said.
Ekran Bhd, the main contractor for a 13.6 billion hydroelectric dam in Malaysia, has awarded 2.4 billion ringgit worth of copper cable contracts for the project over the next five years.
Telekom Malaysia, the national telephone utility, last year projected it will spend a total of 450 million ringgit on copper cables until 1998 to widen its line capacity.

"These contracts don't include deals between cable makers and private telecom companies and independent power producers," Lim said. "If you add those too, you have a market well in excess of eight billion ringgit in the next five years."
A hefty import duty of 30 percent on power cables and 25 percent on telecommunications cables also protects local manufacturers against overseas competition.
"But competition does exist locally and it's very real," said Lim. "There's a tough fight for contracts and that's why statistics are so difficult to obtain."

UBS Securities (Singapore), in a research report on cable-maker Leader Universal Holdings last year, said profit margins were ensured in utility contracts as manufacturers were allowed to impute the actual cost of metals in their quotations.

"Copper and aluminium make up some 70 percent of the cost of sales for cables. The inclusion of this variation enables Leader to pass on any increase in copper or aluminium prices to Telekom and Tenaga," it said.
